## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

The timestamp contract should be corrected because the exposed value and documented NULL semantics misrepresent the supplied event histories.

## Changes
The pull request adds a conditional timestamp column to the process current-state view and documents its meaning in the schema catalog.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — Do not expose a start time as a finish time — For process 20, whose latest event is `started`, this expression exposes its start time as `finished_at`. The catalog defines that column as “Timestamp when the process finished,” but the selected event records a start. — Consumers interpreting this field as documented will incorrectly treat a process with only a start event as finished.
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — Correct the documented meaning of NULL — For process 30, a `started` event followed by `cleared` produces NULL, contradicting “NULL means the process has never been started.” The model checks only the latest event using `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end` (`models/processes.sql:10`). — Consumers using NULL to identify processes that never started will misclassify processes whose latest event is `cleared`.
